lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER V. Advice from a Caterpillar

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Who are you?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar. This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation. Alice replied, rather shyly,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I was when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “What do you mean by that?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar sternly.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Explain yourself!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I can’t explain myself, I’m afraid, sir,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “because I’m not myself, you see.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I don’t see,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’m afraid I can’t put it more clearly,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice replied very politely,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “for I can’t understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It isn’t,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Well, perhaps you haven’t found it so yet,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but when you have to turn into a chrysalis—you will some day, you know—and then after that into a butterfly, I should think you’ll feel it a little queer, won’t you?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Not a bit,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Well, perhaps your feelings may be different,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “all I know is, it would feel very queer to me.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar contemptuously.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Who are you?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Which brought them back again to the beginning of the conversation. Alice felt a little irritated at the Caterpillar’s making such very short remarks, and she drew herself up and said, very gravely,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I think, you ought to tell me who you are, first.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Why?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar. Here was another puzzling question; and as Alice could not think of any good reason, and as the Caterpillar seemed to be in a very unpleasant state of mind, she turned away.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Come back!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Caterpillar called after her.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’ve something important to say!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This sounded promising, certainly: Alice turned and came back again.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Keep your temper,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Is that all?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, swallowing down her anger as well as she could.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “No,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar. Alice thought she might as well wait, as she had nothing else to do, and perhaps after all it might tell her something worth hearing. For some minutes it puffed away without speaking, but at last it unfolded its arms, took the hookah out of its mouth again, and said,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “So you think you’re changed, do you?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’m afraid I am, sir,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I can’t remember things as I used—and I don’t keep the same size for ten minutes together!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Can’t remember what things?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Well, I’ve tried to say “How doth the little busy bee,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: but it all came different!” Alice replied in a very melancholy voice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Repeat, ‘You are old, Father William,’”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar. Alice folded her hands, and began:—

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You are old, Father William,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the young man said,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “And your hair has become very white; And yet you incessantly stand on your head— Do you think, at your age, it is right?”

lines.speaker: Father William
lines.text: “In my youth,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Father William replied to his son,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I feared it might injure the brain; But, now that I’m perfectly sure I have none, Why, I do it again and again.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You are old,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the youth,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “as I mentioned before, And have grown most uncommonly fat; Yet you turned a back-somersault in at the door— Pray, what is the reason of that?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “In my youth,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the sage, as he shook his grey locks,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I kept all my limbs very supple By the use of this ointment—one shilling the box— Allow me to sell you a couple?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You are old,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the youth,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “and your jaws are too weak For anything tougher than suet; Yet you finished the goose, with the bones and the beak— Pray, how did you manage to do it?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “In my youth,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said his father,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I took to the law, And argued each case with my wife; And the muscular strength, which it gave to my jaw, Has lasted the rest of my life.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You are old,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the youth,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “one would hardly suppose That your eye was as steady as ever; Yet you balanced an eel on the end of your nose— What made you so awfully clever?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I have answered three questions, and that is enough,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Said his father;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “don’t give yourself airs! Do you think I can listen all day to such stuff? Be off, or I’ll kick you down stairs!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “That is not said right,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Not quite right, I’m afraid,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, timidly;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “some of the words have got altered.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It is wrong from beginning to end,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar decidedly, and there was silence for some minutes. The Caterpillar was the first to speak.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “What size do you want to be?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: it asked.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Oh, I’m not particular as to size,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice hastily replied;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “only one doesn’t like changing so often, you know.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I don’t know,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar. Alice said nothing: she had never been so much contradicted in her life before, and she felt that she was losing her temper.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Are you content now?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Well, I should like to be a little larger, sir, if you wouldn’t mind,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “three inches is such a wretched height to be.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It is a very good height indeed!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar angrily, rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high).

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “But I’m not used to it!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: pleaded poor Alice in a piteous tone. And she thought of herself,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I wish the creatures wouldn’t be so easily offended!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You’ll get used to it in time,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar; and it put the hookah into its mouth and began smoking again. This time Alice waited patiently until it chose to speak again. In a minute or two the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth and yawned once or twice, and shook itself. Then it got down off the mushroom, and crawled away in the grass, merely remarking as it went,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “One side of what? The other side of what?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: thought Alice to herself.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Of the mushroom,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Caterpillar, just as if she had asked it aloud; and in another moment it was out of sight. Alice remained looking thoughtfully at the mushroom for a minute, trying to make out which were the two sides of it; and as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question. However, at last she stretched her arms round it as far as they would go, and broke off a bit of the edge with each hand.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “And now which is which?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said to herself, and nibbled a little of the right-hand bit to try the effect: the next moment she felt a violent blow underneath her chin: it had struck her foot! She was a good deal frightened by this very sudden change, but she felt that there was no time to be lost, as she was shrinking rapidly; so she set to work at once to eat some of the other bit. Her chin was pressed so closely against her foot, that there was hardly room to open her mouth; but she did it at last, and managed to swallow a morsel of the lefthand bit. * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Come, my head’s free at last!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice in a tone of delight, which changed into alarm in another moment, when she found that her shoulders were nowhere to be found: all she could see, when she looked down, was an immense length of neck, which seemed to rise like a stalk out of a sea of green leaves that lay far below her.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “What can all that green stuff be?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “And where have my shoulders got to? And oh, my poor hands, how is it I can’t see you?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was moving them about as she spoke, but no result seemed to follow, except a little shaking among the distant green leaves. As there seemed to be no chance of getting her hands up to her head, she tried to get her head down to them, and was delighted to find that her neck would bend about easily in any direction, like a serpent. She had just succeeded in curving it down into a graceful zigzag, and was going to dive in among the leaves, which she found to be nothing but the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering, when a sharp hiss made her draw back in a hurry: a large pigeon had flown into her face, and was beating her violently with its wings.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Serpent!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: screamed the Pigeon.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’m not a serpent!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice indignantly.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Let me alone!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Serpent, I say again!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: repeated the Pigeon, but in a more subdued tone, and added with a kind of sob,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’ve tried every way, and nothing seems to suit them!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I haven’t the least idea what you’re talking about,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’ve tried the roots of trees, and I’ve tried banks, and I’ve tried hedges,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Pigeon went on, without attending to her;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but those serpents! There’s no pleasing them!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice was more and more puzzled, but she thought there was no use in saying anything more till the Pigeon had finished.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “As if it wasn’t trouble enough hatching the eggs,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Pigeon;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day! Why, I haven’t had a wink of sleep these three weeks!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’m very sorry you’ve been annoyed,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, who was beginning to see its meaning.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “And just as I’d taken the highest tree in the wood,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: continued the Pigeon, raising its voice to a shriek,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “and just as I was thinking I should be free of them at last, they must needs come wriggling down from the sky! Ugh, Serpent!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “But I’m not a serpent, I tell you!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’m a—I’m a—”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Well! What are you?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Pigeon.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I can see you’re trying to invent something!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I—I’m a little girl,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, rather doubtfully, as she remembered the number of changes she had gone through that day.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “A likely story indeed!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Pigeon in a tone of the deepest contempt.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I’ve seen a good many little girls in my time, but never one with such a neck as that! No, no! You’re a serpent; and there’s no use denying it. I suppose you’ll be telling me next that you never tasted an egg!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I have tasted eggs, certainly,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, who was a very truthful child;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but little girls eat eggs quite as much as serpents do, you know.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I don’t believe it,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Pigeon;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but if they do, why then they’re a kind of serpent, that’s all I can say.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This was such a new idea to Alice, that she was quite silent for a minute or two, which gave the Pigeon the opportunity of adding,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You’re looking for eggs, I know that well enough; and what does it matter to me whether you’re a little girl or a serpent?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It matters a good deal to me,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice hastily;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but I’m not looking for eggs, as it happens; and if I was, I shouldn’t want yours: I don’t like them raw.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Well, be off, then!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Pigeon in a sulky tone, as it settled down again into its nest. Alice crouched down among the trees as well as she could, for her neck kept getting entangled among the branches, and every now and then she had to stop and untwist it. After a while she remembered that she still held the pieces of mushroom in her hands, and she set to work very carefully, nibbling first at one and then at the other, and growing sometimes taller and sometimes shorter, until she had succeeded in bringing herself down to her usual height. It was so long since she had been anything near the right size, that it felt quite strange at first; but she got used to it in a few minutes, and began talking to herself, as usual.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Come, there’s half my plan done now! How puzzling all these changes are! I’m never sure what I’m going to be, from one minute to another! However, I’ve got back to my right size: the next thing is, to get into that beautiful garden—how is that to be done, I wonder?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: As she said this, she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Whoever lives there,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: thought Alice,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “it’ll never do to come upon them this size: why, I should frighten them out of their wits!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So she began nibbling at the righthand bit again, and did not venture to go near the house till she had brought herself down to nine inches high.
